'''Walter L. Craig''' {{post-nominals|country=CAN|FRSC}} (<!--Nov. 28, -->1953 – January 18, 2019)<ref>[https://www.math.mcmaster.ca/index.php/news/department/1919-walter-craig-1953-2019.html Walter Craig 1953 - 2019]</ref> was a United States born Canadian mathematician and a [[Canada Research Chair]] in Mathematical Analysis and Applications at [[McMaster University]], [[Hamilton, Ontario]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca/chairholders-titulaires/profile-eng.aspx?profileId=118 |title=Chairs |publisher=gc.ca |access-date=January 27, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://ms.mcmaster.ca/craig/ |title=Walter Craig |publisher=mcmaster.ca |access-date=January 27, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=l4EkxAMAAAAJ&hl=en |title=Walter Craig |access-date=January 27, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.mcmaster.ca/univsec/reports_lists/DistUnivProf.pdf |title=Distinguished University Professor |publisher=mcmaster.ca |access-date=January 27, 2017}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Craig was born in [[State College, Pennsylvania]] in 1953.  His father, a professor at [[Pennsylvania State University]] transferred to [[University of California, Berkeley]], where Craig and his siblings were raised starting in 1959.

Craig was the son of the logician [[William Craig (philosopher)|William Craig]] and the husband of mathematician [[Deirdre Haskell]].<ref>[https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/celebrating-the-life-of-walter-craig-1953-2019 SIAM News: Celebrating the Life of Walter Craig (1953-2019)]</ref>

== Education ==
Craig attended the University of California at Berkeley and, after spending two years performing as a jazz musician, returned there to graduate with a bachelor's degree in mathematics in 1977.<ref name="AMS">{{cite journal | date=April 2020 | title = Remembrances of Walter Craig| journal = [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] | volume = 67 | issue = 4 | pages = 520–531 | url = https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202004/rnoti-p520.pdf }}</ref> Craig earned his Ph.D. from [[New York University]] - [[Courant Institute]] in 1981; his dissertation, ''A Bifurcation Theory for Periodic Dissipative Wave Equations'', was supervised by [[Louis Nirenberg]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=3333}}</ref>

== Career ==
After stints at the [[California Institute of Technology]], [[Stanford University]], and [[Brown University]], Craig moved to [[McMaster University]] in [[Hamilton, Ontario]], Canada in 2000.  His research topics included [[nonlinear partial differential equation]]s, infinite dimensional [[Hamiltonian system]]s, [[Schrödinger operator]]s and [[spectral theory]], water waves, [[general relativity]], and [[cosmology]].<ref name="AMS" />

In 2007, he was made a [[Fellow]] of the [[Royal Society of Canada]];<ref>{{cite web |url=https://rsc-src.ca/en/search-fellows?keywords_44=&first_name=walter&last_name=craig&display_name=&election_year_21=&academy_25=All&division_24=All&discipline_23=All&is_deceased=0&sort_by=last_name&sort_order=ASC|title=Search Fellows|author=<!--Not stated-->|publisher=[[Royal Society of Canada]]|access-date=September 7, 2017}}</ref> he was awarded a Killam Fellowship in 2009.

In 2013, he became one of the inaugural [[Fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved April 12, 2017</ref> He served as Director of the [[Fields Institute]] from 2013 to 2015.
